record.context_brief: Cardinal symmetry numbers of infinite groups
record.original_question: Let G be an infinite group, and let MS_r(G) and MS_r^+(G) be the cardinal symmetry numbers defined using central symmetries and the cardinal-valued measures card and card^+. Must both MS_r(G) and MS_r^+(G) be infinite for every finite number of colors r? Equivalently, does every finite coloring of an infinite group contain monochromatic symmetric subsets of arbitrarily large finite size?

evidence.quote: We shall be interested in the maximal symmetry numbers msr(G, card, S) and msr(G, card+, S) of groups G endowed with the family S = {sc : c ∈ G} of central symmetries sc : x 7→ cx−1c. These symmetry Ramsey numbers will be denoted by MSr(G) and MS+r(G), respectively, and will be referred to as cardinal symmetry numbers of G.

Problem 8.4 (Protasov). Are the cardinals MSr(G) and MS+r(G) infinite for every infinite group G and every finite cardinal r? Equivalently, is it true that for every finite coloring of an infinite group G there exist a monochromatic symmetric subset A ⊂ G of arbitrary large finite cardinality?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be an infinite group. For each element $c\in G$, define the central symmetry $s_c:G\to G$ by $s_c(x)=cx^{-1}c$, and let $\mathcal S=\{s_c:c\in G\}$. A subset $A\subseteq G$ is called symmetric if $s_c(A)=A$ for some $c\in G$.

For a positive integer $r$ and a coloring $\chi:G\to\{1,\dots,r\}$, let
$$\mathrm{ms}_r(G,\chi)=\sup\{|A|:A\subseteq G\text{ is symmetric and monochromatic with respect to }\chi\}\in\mathrm{Card}\cup\{\infty\},$$
where $|A|$ is the cardinality of $A$. Define
$$MS_r(G)=\min_{\chi:G\to\{1,\dots,r\}}\sup\{|A|:A\subseteq G\text{ symmetric, }\chi\text{-monochromatic}\}$$
(using ordinary cardinality $\operatorname{card}$), and let $MS_r^+(G)$ be the analogous quantity defined with the strict-cardinality measure $\operatorname{card}^+$ (which assigns to a set $A$ the smallest cardinal strictly greater than $|A|$).

Question: For every infinite group $G$ and every finite cardinal $r\ge 1$, are both $MS_r(G)$ and $MS_r^+(G)$ infinite? Equivalently, must every coloring $\chi:G\to\{1,\dots,r\}$ of an infinite group $G$ in finitely many colors admit monochromatic symmetric subsets of arbitrarily large finite cardinality?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface related work by Banakh, Verbitsky, Vorobets and Protasov on monochromatic symmetric subsets of colored groups, including results for infinite Abelian groups (where finite colorings yield large monochromatic symmetric subsets) and computations of ν(ℤᵏ)=k+1. However, no source was found that explicitly resolves the general question for arbitrary infinite (possibly non-abelian) groups with the central symmetries s_c(x)=cx⁻¹c. The status appears to remain unresolved in full generality.

status_evidence.title: A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses symmetry numbers ms_r and the family of central symmetries on groups; treats Abelian and Euclidean cases.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational framework for the problem; does not state a resolution of Problem 8.4 in the general (non-abelian) setting.

status_evidence.title: Monochrome symmetric subsets of colored groups - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: For any finite coloring of an infinite Abelian group G of cardinality > κ, G contains a monochromatic symmetric subset of cardinality ≥ κ.
status_evidence.claim: Resolves the abelian case but not the general infinite-group case.
